children: McDonald's Corp. (MCD, Financials), the global restaurant chain known for its franchise-heavy business model, has reached a milestone few companies manage to achieve.
The company raised its quarterly dividend to $1.93 a share, up from $1.86.
That increase is fairly modest. The streak behind it is much more interesting.
McDonald's has now increased its dividend for 50 consecutive years, putting half a century of uninterrupted annual dividend growth behind the company.
At the new payout, the stock carries a forward yield of about 3.1%.
The dividend will be paid Dec. 15 to shareholders of record Dec. 1. The stock will also trade ex-dividend on Dec. 1. The increase comes at a more challenging point for McDonald's.

Its shares have recently traded near 52-week lows as investors watch slowing comparable sales and tougher competition across the restaurant industry. McDonald's has been leaning more heavily on value offerings as it tries to keep price-conscious customers coming through its restaurants.
That makes the 50-year milestone particularly notable.
McDonald's has kept raising its payout through very different economic environments. The next test is whether its underlying business can regain enough momentum to keep that record going comfortably.

title: McDonald's just gave income investors another reason to pay attention
